_RULES_FOR_THE_NEXT_AGENT: FORMAT = '29aug' (words use term/translation, lines are plain strings, scenes are objects). This is what the deployed pipeline (pipeline.py normalize -> tts_29.py / flux_gen_opt.py / assemble_29.py / ltx_29.py) is built around. Do NOT invent new keys.

RULE 1 (prevents the collapse): words[].term is ALWAYS the FOREIGN (non-English) word and words[].translation is ALWAYS the English meaning - in ALL SIX channels, INCLUDING english-to-arabic / english-to-chinese / english-to-spanish. The channel name NEVER flips the direction. English text inside 'term' = broken reel (0-byte TTS -> assemble crash -> the whole 12-reel group gets skipped).
RULE 2: lines[] = exactly 3 plain ENGLISH narration strings (hook question, fact, call-to-action). Not objects. No foreign text in lines.

RULE 3: scenes[] = exactly 4 objects with keys scene_index, shot_type, ltx_motion_profile, prompt. 'prompt' is an English image prompt (subject/setting/lighting) ending with ', cinematic film still, vertical composition'. NEVER write 'LTX motion:' inside prompt - the pipeline appends that marker itself. 'ltx_motion_profile' holds ONLY the motion/physics description.

RULE 4: voices are FIXED per channel - copy them exactly from the example reel of the same channel. voice_src = FROM-language voice, voice_tgt = TO-language voice (for english-to-* channels voice_src is the English voice on purpose - the pipeline swaps it).
RULE 5: exactly 3 words, 3 lines, 4 scenes per reel. words[].translit optional (Latin reading of the term) - keep it for ar/zh.
RULE 6: 12 reels per JSON file, 2 files per job. Same 29aug format in every reel of both files - never mix with the old aug28 src/tgt format.

RULE 7: topic = fresh kebab-case slug never used before (pipeline dedups against all past manifests). id/pair/seed are re-assigned by the pipeline - placeholders are fine. music = one short English mood string.

FINAL SELF-CHECK: for every english-to-* reel, read each words[].term - if it is English, you inverted the direction. Fix before submitting. (ar/zh terms must be non-Latin script; es terms are Spanish words.)
